marks.gloss_en: דתניא: a man read הודע את ירושלים before R' Eliezer, who rebuked him -- go examine your mother's abominations -- and they found a taint of unfitness in him: the source for R' Eliezer's view that the clause excludes
'Make known to Jerusalem her abominations' (Ezekiel 16:2) is read and translated
the incident of Lot and his two daughters is read and translated
the incident of Tamar and Yehuda is read and translated
the first [account of the] incident of the Calf is read and translated
the curses and blessings are read and translated
the warnings and punishments are read and translated
the incident of Amnon and Tamar is read and translated
the incident of the concubine in Giv'a is read and translated
the Priestly Benediction is read [in the Torah reading] but not translated [into the targum]
townspeople who sold the town square buy a synagogue with its proceeds
והא אמרת מעשה אמנון ותמר נקרא ומתרגם! -- the Tosefta has the Amnon story read and translated, yet the mishnah says not read (kind tanya stands in for והא אמרת; header)

לא קשיא: הא דכתיב אמנון בן דוד, הא דכתיב אמנון סתמא -- the mishnah speaks of the verses naming him 'son of David', the Tosefta of those naming him plain 'Amnon' (= p_okimta_amnon_ben_david, p_okimta_amnon_stama)
the incident of David and Amnon is neither read nor translated (the lemma's reading; 25a.16 prints נקראין ולא מתרגמין -- header)
all verses written in the Torah coarsely are read refinedly: yishgalena as yishkavena, bafolim as batechorim, chiryonim as divyonim, choreihem / meimei shineihem as tzo'atam / meimei ragleihem
the baraita: lemacharaot ('latrines', 2 Kgs 10:27) is read lemotza'ot
Rav Nachman: all mockery is forbidden
a Jew is permitted to say to a gentile: take the idol and put it in its shin-tav
שמתוך תשובה שהשיבו אהרן למשה פקרו המערערים -- the ground R' Shimon ben Elazar gives for his dictum
R' Shimon ben Elazar: a person should always be careful in his answers
and these are read and not translated: the incident of Reuven is read and not translated
the second incident of the Calf is read and not translated
